newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Three shortlisted for Ivorian telecoms sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Three shortlisted for Ivorian telecoms sell-off.

text.p: Three consortia involving rival French, Malaysian and U.S. interests have been shortlisted for the battle to take over Ivory Coast's phone monopoly CI-TELCOM. A fourth could still join the race.

A cabinet statement, published in the government daily Fraternite Matin on Saturday, named the three front-runners as France-Telecom, Telekom Malaysia and Africa Bell, a consortium of Ivorian and U.S. interests.
The fourth group, GS Holding, must provide further information to the privatisation committee, the statement said. Details of its make-up were not immediately available.
The shortlisted consortia, in which Ivorian companies must have a stake of between 10 and 15 percent, have until the end of November to submit their bids.

The winner will take a 51 to 55 percent stake, the state will retain 35 percent, eight to 10 percent will be sold to Ivorian shareholders on the Abidjan stock exchange and staff will be offered one to two percent.

France-Telecom, which is bidding through a local subsidiary including Ivorian commodities giant, SIFCOM, has historical ties to the former French colony and is a major provider of international circuits and technical services to CI-TELCOM.
CI-TELCOM owes it the bulk of a total debt estimated independently at hundreds of millions of dollars.

U.S. industry sources said major U.S. carriers, notably AT&T and MCI Communications Corp who have international circuits into Ivory Coast, showed initial interest in the bid but eventually backed out mainly because of the cost.
Estimates of the total value of CI-TELCOM range from $200 million to $350 million.
